root_cause.text: The TLS RX async decrypt path leaked cloned encrypted skbs because `tls_sw_recvmsg()` did not always purge `ctx->async_hold` after `tls_strp_msg_hold()` failed and `tls_decrypt_sg()` waited for completion, leaving pinned skbs queued with no later free path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold)` from `tls_sw_recvmsg()` into `tls_decrypt_async_wait()` and the commit message explicitly says this “fixes a leak when tls_strp_msg_hold() fails part-way through” because `tls_sw_recvmsg()` “only flushes the async_hold queue when one record has been processed in ‘fully-async’ mode,” which may not happen.

intent_record.intent_summary: Purge the TLS async hold queue after waiting for decryption to complete to avoid leaving stale packets queued.
intent_record.what: In `tls_decrypt_async_wait(struct tls_sw_context_rx *ctx)`, a call to `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold);` was inserted immediately before the function returns `ctx->async_wait.err`.
intent_record.how: This change clears all sk_buffs currently queued on `ctx->async_hold` whenever the async decrypt wait path completes, preventing previously held packets from remaining queued across this point in the receive/decrypt flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop prematurely purging the async hold queue in `tls_sw_recvmsg()` after waiting for async decryption.
intent_record.what: A call to `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold);` was removed from `tls_sw_recvmsg()` immediately after `tls_decrypt_async_wait(ctx);` and before the error check on `ret`.
intent_record.how: The function no longer unconditionally empties the `async_hold` skb queue at that point in the receive path. This preserves the queued skbs after waiting for asynchronous decryption, rather than discarding them regardless of whether decryption completed successfully or returned an error.

grouping_result.intent: Stop prematurely purging the async hold queue in `tls_sw_recvmsg()` after waiting for async decryption.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix TLS receive handling so the async hold queue is purged only after async decryption has completed, preventing stale queued packets.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the reported TLS RX async decrypt leak by fixing when `ctx->async_hold` is purged in `tls_sw_recvmsg()`, ensuring queued cloned skbs are not left pinned after async decryption handling.

candidates.rationale: This purge was executed immediately after waiting for async decryption, but the root cause says the queue was not always purged at the correct time when `tls_strp_msg_hold()` failed and `tls_decrypt_sg()` was still pending. Purging here is the vulnerable behavior because it occurs in the wrong place relative to async completion handling.

This wait is the control point for the async decrypt path. The bug manifests because `tls_sw_recvmsg()` relied on this wait but did not consistently follow it with the correct async_hold cleanup, leaving cloned encrypted skbs queued.

This indicates the async decrypt completion wait in the TLS RX path. The vulnerability stems from the fact that waiting for completion alone did not guarantee queued cloned skbs were purged, allowing leaks when later cleanup was skipped.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the vulnerable cleanup site in tls_sw_recvmsg(): the fix intent says purge was happening at the wrong time after async decryption waiting. The root cause is that cloned encrypted skbs in ctx->async_hold were not always purged when tls_strp_msg_hold() failed and tls_decrypt_sg() was still pending, causing the leak.

This wait governs the async RX decrypt completion path. By itself it did not ensure ctx->async_hold was later purged in all failure/early-exit cases, which is the condition that left cloned skbs pinned and leaked.

This is the async completion wait in the TLS RX decryption path. The vulnerability arises because waiting for crypto completion did not guarantee queued cloned skbs were freed, enabling leakage when later purge handling was skipped.

commit c618db2afe7c31d13ca8cf05b60f17165fbdc282
Author: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu Jul 14 22:22:33 2022 -0700

    tls: rx: async: hold onto the input skb
    
    Async crypto currently benefits from the fact that we decrypt
    in place. When we allow input and output to be different skbs
    we will have to hang onto the input while we move to the next
    record. Clone the inputs and keep them on a list.
    
    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
    Signed-of
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the post-fix behavior, not the vulnerable one. In `tls_decrypt_sg()` the async path now explicitly clones/holds the input skb: `if (unlikely(darg->async)) { err = tls_strp_msg_hold(sk, skb, &ctx->async_hold); if (err) __skb_queue_tail(&ctx->async_hold, darg->skb); return err; }`. In `tls_sw_recvmsg()` it also purges the hold queue after waiting for async completion: `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold);`. This directly addresses the reported leak of cloned encrypted skbs being left in `ctx->async_hold` after async decrypt. Since the vulnerable construct is the missing purge/hold-handling, and this code already contains the corrective handling, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
